title: Montesquieu
summary: Charles-Louis de Secondat, baron de La Brede et de Montesquieu (1689-1755), was born into a noble family near Bordeaux and inherited the barony of La Brede. After the Persian Letters he published The Spirit of the Laws in 1748, arguing that laws should fit each people's government, climate, economy and customs, and that liberty is best protected when separate bodies hold legislative, executive and judicial power. This separation of powers shaped liberal political theory and the framers of the United States Constitution. He died in Paris.

uncertainty.note: Born 18 January 1689 (baptised 19 January) at La Brède; died 10 February 1755 in Paris.

as_recorded.value: In 1755, Montesquieu died of a fever in Paris
